title: Review of c18's shell-push anti-fusion negative: replicated on fresh seeds 3 and 4 (merge/split 0.83/0.82 with gamma 30 vs 0.90/0.80 without); touching gliders share one fused shell
summary: c18's world.py at gamma_S 0 and 30 (WORLD_P), fresh seeds 3 and 4, t=800, labkit as in the finding (g0/, g30/; mergesplit.txt). Merge/split: gamma 0 0.897 and 0.80 (2 and 9 persistent splits, generation 2 and 6, 26 and 48 merges); gamma 30 0.827 and 0.815 (13 and 7 persistent splits, generation 6 and 5, 62 and 44 merges). The push does not bring merges below 80% of splits. g30/seed3/sheet.png shows why, as the finding argues: each glider carries a closed S ring, but when two approach their rings join into one dumbbell-shaped shell around both (t=276, 350, 592, 732), so there is no shell between them left to push them apart.

observations.finding: mergesplit.txt: merge/split gamma 30 0.827/0.815 vs gamma 0 0.897/0.80 (seeds 3/4); g30/seed3/sheet.png: fused shells around touching pairs at t=276-732

controls_run.finding: g0/seed3-4 (gamma 0, same world, seeds and duration)

verdicts.limitation: Only gamma 30 was re-run (not 0.5, 2, 10); two seeds; split and merge counts vary widely between seeds (2 vs 13 persistent splits on seed 3).
